messages:
jonathan: Heads-up: after merging PR #1248 (a1b2c3d4) I'm seeing a clear latency regression on the serving runtime for long-context streaming. Median token latency for our rn50-llama variant went from ~12ms/token -> ~22ms/token in steady-state. This started ~after the kernel-selection heuristic change that prefers the new "large-grid" GEMM kernels.
maria: Ugh. Can you attach traces (nsys / perfetto) and the nvprof summary? :eyes:
jonathan: Yep. I captured an nsys profile on the failing build and the previous tag (v2024-05-01). Commands I used:
```
# record (30s warmup + 60s sampling)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --sample=none --output=/tmp/nsys_june1 "python server.py --workload=real_traffic"
# perfetto upload to share
python tools/trace_upload.py /tmp/perfetto_trace.pb --out=https://perfetto.google.com/trace/ABCDEFG
```
And a quick nvprof-like kernel summary (nsys exported):
```
Before (v2024-05-01):
matmul_tiled_v1  total_time  58.2ms   calls  1200  avg 48.5us
softmax_fused     total_time  12.6ms   calls  1200  avg 10.5us

After (post-PR #1248):
matmul_tiled_v2  total_time  128.4ms  calls 1200  avg 106.9us  <-- big jump
softmax_fused    total_time  14.1ms   calls 1200  avg 11.7us
```
maria: matmul_tiled_v2 is the new kernel selector target, right? That doubling in total_time stands out. Any difference in sequence length / batch distribution between runs?
jonathan: Good call. I dug into request traces — average decode seq_len at the time of capture changed from ~32 -> ~48 (we had a short blip of longer requests). That affects the tiling choice because the heuristic picks larger grid kernels for longer seqs. But still, even with same seq_len the kernel is slower on average.
perf-bot: Automated perf summary (nsys_export):
- p50 latency before: 12.1ms
- p50 latency after: 21.9ms
- p95 before: 28.7ms
- p95 after: 45.1ms
- top hotspot: matmul_tiled_v2 (49% of GPU time)

dena: Can we bisect the change quickly? If PR #1248 touched kernel_selector.cpp that's the likely culprit. Suggest `git bisect` between v2024-05-01..HEAD and run a short perf harness that reproduces the regression.
jonathan: I started a bisect job on a ci-worker. Repro script:
```
# reproducer (30s)
./tools/run_repro.sh \
  --model=rn50-llama --bs=1 --streaming=true --runtime-config=ci/heavy_seq.json
```
Bisect command I ran on the worker:
```
git bisect start HEAD v2024-05-01
git bisect run ./tools/ci_bisect_runner.sh
```
Got an interesting hit: commit 4f2e9b7 changed `kernel_selector::score_grid` to bias +10% for grids that reduce kernel launches but didn't account for active_kv_cache length.
maria: If the heuristic is biasing toward fewer kernel launches, maybe it prefers a kernel with higher occupancy startup cost that amortizes poorly for cached KV small-step runs.
jonathan: Exactly. I compared perfetto timelines for matmul kernels. Before: many short matmul_tiled_v1 kernels with high occupancy util but low latency; After: fewer, larger matmul_tiled_v2 calls that have higher per-call latency. Timeline snippets (perfetto flame slice simplified):
```
Before timeline: [matmul_tiled_v1: 0.05ms] x 1200 -> interleaved softmax/kv ops
After timeline:  [matmul_tiled_v2: 0.11ms] x 1200 -> longer blocks, overlaps less with async copy
```
sre-alex: Also check memory copy overlap and whether the new kernel blocks the copy streams. I saw the nsys timeline show compute stream 0 hogging GPU and async-copy stream 2 stalled during many tiles.
jonathan: Good catch. I added `--dump-kvcache-stats` to the repro and saw cache hit ratio normal (~97%) but the KV cache average length increase means the per-step matmul dimensions changed and the selector switched kernels. Quick experiment: reran the repro with KV cache disabled (`--kv-cache=off`) and the regression went away (p50 back to ~12.3ms). So it's an interaction between kernel selection and KV cache behavior.
dena: That narrows it down. Two short-term options: revert the heuristic change (safe) or update the selector to consider `active_kv_cache_len` and the cost model for amortization/overlap.
maria: Do we have a model of kernel startup cost vs per-element time? If we can fit a simple linear cost model (startup + per-MAC cost) we can pick the kernel by expected time = startup + per_op * Nops where Nops ~ seq_len*hidden*... We should also account for overlap with copies - add a penalty when copy-util is high.
jonathan: I profiled kernels with microbench to get startup/per-op numbers:
```
matmul_tiled_v1: startup 2.4us, per-MAC 0.00073ns
matmul_tiled_v2: startup 9.8us, per-MAC 0.00065ns
```
For short cached steps v1 is still better. The PR's +10% bias pushed the threshold to prefer v2 even when seq_len ~40.
perf-bot: CI bisect result: commit 4f2e9b7 identified as first bad commit. Link: https://ci.redwood/compare/4f2e9b7
maria: Plan: revert the +10% bias in the heuristic (hotfix), and simultaneously add unit tests for selector decision boundaries including active_kv_cache_len scenarios. Dena, can you open a hotfix PR to revert? I'll draft the improved cost model for follow-up.
dena: On it. I'll open redwood/runtime#1257 reverting the bias and add a regression test that runs the reproducer with --kv-cache on/off.
jonathan: Thanks all. After my local revert test, p50 returns to 12.2ms and p95 to 29ms. I'll keep the nsys/perfetto captures uploaded here for reference: https://perfetto.google.com/trace/ABCDEFG (after) and https://perfetto.google.com/trace/HIJKLMN (before). :white_check_mark:
maria: Awesome. Follow-up items:
- (maria) implement cost model + overlap penalty (PR)
- (dena) hotfix revert PR + regression test
- (jonathan) add CI nsys smoke to catch large kernel-shift regressions
- (sre-alex) add a perf alert that watches kernel composition (%) changes per deployment
sre-alex: I'll add a Grafana rule to emit an alert when any single kernel's GPU time fraction increases >20% vs baseline. Helps catch these earlier.
jonathan: Thanks everyone. Leaving the traces and bisect logs in /artifacts/perf/1719823456-bisect/ if you need raw captures.
maria: Nice debugging. Great example of selector interacting with KV cache. :clap:
